replication.target_description: Experiment 4 Part 1, Hypothesis 1: perceived agency index in Sexual versus Clothed conditions; independent-samples Welch’s t, two-tailed, main full-sample analysis. Matched by outcome, conditions, and supplied Table 9 locator.

n.sample_role: Participants contributing agency index scores to the independent Sexual versus Clothed contrast (335 Sexual; 338 Clothed).
n.exclusions: Main analysis uses the full sample before supplementary exclusions. Naked condition (336 participants) is outside this contrast. Supplementary post-exclusion analysis is separate: 56 exclusions across all conditions; Sexual 321 and Clothed 315.
n.location: Main manuscript p. 42, Table 10 contrast header and note; corroborated by p. 30 Table 9 and p. 31 Hypothesis 1. Supplementary pp. 34, 37–39 distinguish exclusion analysis.
n.quote: Independent samples t-test: Contrast between Sexual Condition (335) and Clothed Condition (338) ... Note. Welch’s t (two-tailed) for independent samples, N = 673.

notes: Identity assessment: canonical text opens with “Revisiting the link between Mind Perception and Objectification: Replication and Extension of Gray et al (2011)”, authored by Tsz Ching (Ivard) Tsang and Gilad Feldman. It identifies itself as a preliminary MSc-thesis preprint, reports completed data collection and results, cites the exact Gray et al. original DOI 10.1037/a0025883, and links https://osf.io/w34fb and https://osf.io/8hdu3/ on main p. 17; supplementary p. 3 also links the supplied registration. Thus this is the primary replication report associated with that registration, rather than the registration itself. No PDF was supplied. Only n_r is assigned. The supplied Table 9 locator identifies the main full-sample analysis; its main-text Hypothesis 1 and Table 10 confirm the exact agency contrast. Analytic N = 673 is explicitly printed, independently consistent with 335 + 338 = 673 mutually exclusive between-subjects condition participants; this is not the whole-study N = 1009 and does not include Naked-condition participants. Supplementary post-exclusion variant is documented separately (321 + 315 = 636); not substituted for the main Table 9 analysis. The main model intentionally uses pre-exclusion data, as specified in supplementary p. 34. Unassigned original, effect size, p, and success fields are placeholders only and must not overwrite previously verified fields.
